Tinsley played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. Following his senior year, he was drafted by the [[Vancouver Grizzlies]] with the 27th pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]] and was immediately dealt to the [[Atlanta Hawks]], and then to the [[Indiana Pacers]] on draft night. Tinsley played 11 seasons in the NBA, primarily with the Pacers, as well as the Grizzlies and Jazz. ==Early years and college career== As a teen, Tinsley developed his game playing [[streetball]] at New York City's [[Rucker Park]]. Tinsley's streetball nickname is "Mel The Abuser". He played junior college ball at [[Mt. San Jacinto College]] (MSJC) before breaking onto the national scene in the [[Big 12 Conference]] at [[Iowa State University]].[http://www.brooklynusa.org/espn1.htm Breaking Away: The Jamaal Tinsley Story] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071015115929/http://brooklynusa.org/espn1.htm |date=October 15, 2007 }} In Tinsley's junior year with the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclones]], he was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]]. He led Iowa State to a No. 2 seed in the [[2000 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. The team, along with fellow star [[Marcus Fizer]], reached the Elite Eight before losing to eventual champion Michigan State. In his senior year, Tinsley earned first-team [[2001 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors from the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]]. ==NBA career== ===Indiana Pacers (2001–2009)=== [[File:Tinsley pacers jersey.jpg|thumb|left|Tinsley wore #11 during his tenure at Iowa State and while with the Indiana Pacers.]] Tinsley established himself as the starting point guard under Pacers coach [[Isiah Thomas]]. He put up statistics of 9.4 points and 8.1 assists per game in [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02]]. On November 16, 2001, he recorded the 9th [[Double (basketball)#Five-by-five|five-by-five]] in the NBA since the 1985–86 season.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200111160IND.html] Basketball-Reference, September 12, 2014 At 23 years and 261 days, he was the youngest to do so until Andrei Kirilenko in 2003. Tinsley played 73 games for the Pacers in [[2002–03 NBA season|2002–03]], starting 69 of them, and his averages dipped to 7.8 points and 7.5 assists per contest.{{cite web|title=Jamaal Tinsley bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jamaal_tinsley/bio.html|publisher=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725002131/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jamaal_tinsley/bio.html|archive-date=July 25, 2008}} The following year, [[Rick Carlisle]] replaced Thomas as the Pacers' head coach, and promoted veteran guard [[Kenny Anderson (basketball)|Kenny Anderson]] to the starting point guard slot, with [[Anthony Johnson (basketball)|Anthony Johnson]] as his backup. When Anderson and Johnson went down with injuries, Tinsley regained his status as a starter. As the Pacers advanced to the [[2004 NBA Playoffs#Conference Finals|2004 Eastern Conference Finals]], Tinsley started all 16 playoff games. Tinsley spent the majority of the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] on injured reserve due to a bruised left foot, but the team played its way to a 44–38 record and the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference. Tinsley missed the first four games of the Pacers' first-round series against the [[Boston Celtics]], but made a return in a Game 5 victory. In that game on May 3, 2005, Tinsley made seven assists, five steals, and six points, and the five steals tied the most among all players during the 2005 postseason and his personal best for the playoffs. Tinsley's injury problems continued during the 2007–08 season; he only played in 39 games, during which he averaged a career-high 8.4 assists. For the 2008–09 season, Tinsley was replaced in the starting lineup by point guard [[T. J. Ford]]. O'Brien and Pacers' President of Basketball Operations [[Larry Bird]] told Tinsley he would not play for the Pacers again and would be traded as soon as possible, then shipped his personal items to Tinsley's home in Atlanta. Tinsley then requested a contract buyout through his agent.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3880962 Jamaal Tinsley, Players Association to File Grievance] ESPN.com, February 3, 2009 Because of the situation where Indiana's insistence on trading and not outright waiving Tinsley meant that no other team offered Indiana anything of value to acquire him (knowing that the Pacers would eventually have to part ways with Tinsley and then he could be picked up at no cost), the NBA Players Association filed a grievance against the Pacers on Tinsley's behalf on February 11, 2009.[https://news.yahoo.com/s/afp/20090211/sp_afp/basketnbapacerstinsley;_ylt=AkLsbkyuvDigvPrERdHUrGa79LQF Players Association Files Grievance Over Inactivity] Yahoo! Sports, February 12, 2009 On July 22, 2009, the Pacers waived Tinsley.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/tinsley_090722.html |title=Pacers, Tinsley reach resolution |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 22, 2009 |access-date=November 15, 2009}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2009–2010)=== On November 14, 2009, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] signed Tinsley as a free agent.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_sign_jamaal_tinsley_091114.html |title=Grizzlies sign Jamaal Tinsley |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=November 14, 2009 |access-date=November 15, 2009}} [[Chris Wallace (NBA general manager)|Chris Wallace]], the General Manager of the Grizzlies, stated that he "was the best available player out on the board" and was "a proven commodity as a playmaker" due to his veteran resume in the NBA.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4654711 |title=Grizzlies add Tinsley to backcourt |date=November 14, 2009 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 14, 2009}} ===Los Angeles D-Fenders (2011)=== On November 3, 2011, Tinsley was picked 1st overall by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] in the NBA Development League Draft.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2011/index.html 2011 D-League Draft] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111207031237/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2011/index.html |date=December stats|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/jamaal_tinsley/career_stats.html|publisher=NBA Development League|access-date=December 23, (2011–2013)=== On December 12, 2011, Tinsley was signed by the Utah Jazz, along with [[Keith McLeod]], and [[Trey Gilder]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz_signs_tinsley_mcleod_glider.html|title=Jazz Signs Jamaal Tinsley, Keith McLeod and Trey Gilder |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=December 12, 2011 |access-date=January 24, 2013}} On June 29, 2012, the Jazz exercised the team option on Tinsley's contract to keep him under contract for one more season.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/20120629-tinsley-evans-options.html|title=Jazz Exercises Team Option on Tinsley for 2012-13, Makes Qualifying Offer to Evans |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 29, 2012 |access-date=January 24, 2013}} On October 26, 2013, he re-signed with the Jazz.{{cite web | title = Jazz Signs Guard Jamaal Tinsley | url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-guard-jamaal-tinsley |work=NBA.com |date=October 26, 2013 |access-date=October 26, 2013}} He would only play 8 games with the team and on November 12, 2013, he was waived by the Jazz.{{cite web | title = Jazz Waives Guard
